title: I'm Not Scared, You're Scared!
author: Seth Meyers
intro: Bear gets scared very easily, even of his own reflection in the mirror. Luckily, his best friend Rabbit is very brave!
checkedAgainst: Storyline Online page and teacher guide

questions.q: Who is the main character who gets scared easily?
questions.clue: He is a big furry animal who loves staying safe at home.
questions.yes: Bear is the main character who gets scared easily.

questions.q: Who is Bear's very brave best friend?
questions.clue: She has long, strong ears and hops around.
questions.yes: Rabbit is Bear's very brave best friend.

questions.q: Why does Bear tie a bell to his door every night?

options.text: To hear if anyone sneaks inside

questions.clue: He is a heavy sleeper and wants a warning sound.
questions.yes: Bear ties a bell to his door in case anyone sneaks in.

questions.q: What does Rabbit tell Bear they are going to do together?

options.text: Paint all the walls in the house

questions.clue: Rabbit wants them to go outside and explore new places.
questions.yes: Rabbit tells Bear they are going on an adventure.

questions.q: What would Bear rather do at home to stay safe?

options.text: Read a book about adventures instead

questions.clue: He says they can just close the pages if anything goes wrong.
questions.yes: Bear would rather stay home and read a book about adventures.

questions.q: Where do Bear and Rabbit stop at their first obstacle?
questions.clue: Bear worries that cold water and sharp-toothed fish are inside it.
questions.yes: Bear and Rabbit stop at a small stream first.

questions.q: How does Bear get past the dark and spooky woods?

options.text: He sails in a big wooden boat

questions.clue: He walks to the road and waits at a stop for a vehicle.
questions.yes: Bear waits by the road and takes a bus around the woods.

questions.q: What does Bear ride to reach the top of the mountain?

options.text: A train and then a helicopter

questions.clue: First he goes to a station, and then he flies from an airfield.
questions.yes: Bear takes a train and a helicopter to the top of the mountain.

questions.q: What is Rabbit doing every time Bear catches up with her?
questions.clue: Bear takes so long that she closes her eyes and naps.
questions.yes: Rabbit has fallen asleep waiting for Bear each time.

questions.q: What makes Bear finally admit he is scared and go home?

options.text: A long, old, rickety rope bridge

questions.clue: It stretches across a gap and has old wooden boards.
questions.yes: Bear admits he is scared of the long, old, rickety bridge.

questions.q: Why does the board on the bridge crack under Rabbit?

options.text: She jumps up and down on it

questions.clue: She bounces hard to prove that the bridge is safe.
questions.yes: The board cracks because Rabbit jumps hard up and down on it.

questions.q: How does Rabbit feel while hanging from the broken bridge?
questions.clue: She is holding on by her ears and knows she will slip soon.
questions.yes: Rabbit feels scared for the first time in her life.

questions.q: Who flies to Bear's house and rings the bell to wake him?
questions.clue: This little feathered creature followed them on their whole journey.
questions.yes: A small bird shakes the bell on Bear's doorknob to wake him.

questions.q: Why does Bear run through the stream and woods and climb the mountain?

options.text: To catch the last helicopter home

questions.clue: He is worried about his friend hanging from the bridge.
questions.yes: Bear faces all his fears to run back and rescue Rabbit.

questions.q: How does Bear feel after he pulls Rabbit to safety?
questions.clue: He did something very brave to save his best friend.
questions.yes: Bear feels proud and sees a brave bear in the mirror.
